question.text:
You are evaluating the financial performance of two retail chains based on their profitability ratios: Chain A: Return on Assets (ROA) = 10%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 15% Chain B: Return on Assets (ROA) = 12%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 18%
Rank the chains based on profitability.

answer.text: Both chains have the same profitability
Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Profitability is read off ROA and ROE together. Chain B wins on both — ROA 12% vs 10% and ROE 18% vs 15% — so Chain B is the more profitable retailer. The Trap: Picking Chain A ignores both ratios; 'same profitability' ignores a clean 2-percentage-point lead on each measure; 'cannot determine' wrongly demands margin or turnover disclosures when ROA/ROE already settle the ranking. Cross-Exam Context: ROA/ROE comparison is tested in NISM XV, X-A and XXI-B as part of portfolio-company screening. Distributor's Pro-Tip: When a client asks 'why did my PMS buy this retailer over that one', pull out ROA + ROE — HNI clients understand 'return on the money the company uses' far better than EV/EBITDA.
